سَكٌّ A nail; a pin, or peg, of iron; as also ↓ سَكِىٌّ ; (S, K;) like as one says دَوٌّ and دَوِىٌّ: (S:) pl. سِكَاكٌ (S, K) and سُكُوكٌ. (K.) [A verse of Aboo-Dahbal El-Jumahee is cited as an ex. in the TA as follows: “دِرْعِى دِلَاصٌ سَكُّهَا سَكٌّ عَجَبْ
وَجَوْبُهَا القَاتِرُ مِنْ سَيرِ اليَلَبْ
” but see يَلَبٌ.] ＝
-A2- A straight, or an even, building, and excavation, (O, K,) like a wall, without curvity, or bending. (O.) ―
-b2- A coat of mail narrow in the rings; (S, K;) as also ↓ سُكٌّ , and ↓ سَكَّآءُ : (K:) or, accord. to the O, soft in the rings. (TA.) ―
-b3- See also the next paragraph.
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
